# Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes (German Academic Scholarship Foundation)
Founded originally in Dresden in 1925, the Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes was re-established as a registered association in Cologne in 1948 after being dissolved in 1934 under National Socialism. It is Germany's largest and most prestigious scholarship foundation, offering financial and academic support to highly talented undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral students. Admission is merit-based and conducted via multiple nomination channels, including school principals, university professors, examination boards, competitions, an assessment test, alumni nominations, and specialized arts nominations. The selection focuses on excellence, initiative, and responsibility, with no citizenship or age restrictions.
The scholarship provides monthly financial allowances covering living expenses and insurance, with additional need-based support and funding for study abroad and tuition fees. Academic support includes summer schools, workshops, research groups, mentoring, and funding for scholar-organized events. As of 2023, approximately 14,888 students were supported, representing around 0.48% of the student population in Germany. Notable alumni include multiple Nobel laureates, Fields Medalists, and leading figures across sciences, social sciences, business, politics, arts, and journalism. Internal and open scholarship programs operate in partnership with institutions like KAUST and support areas such as research internships and music composition.
